role.altitude: The dermatologist keeps examining, diagnosing, treating, operating and counselling; searching image archives, retyping medication and answers, and typing histories and notes shrink.
skills_to_grow: Correcting scribe drafts quickly and carefully
role.ambitious_version: A dermatologist whose time goes to patients, not typing.

tasks.short: Examine pigmented lesions with the dermatoscope and talk with the patient, take dermoscopy images, find earlier images of the same lesion, decide diagnosis and treatment, perform excisions and biopsies, write findings and plan, fill the pathology request and answer patient messages.

steps.what: Dermatologist examines pigmented lesions such as nevi or melanoma with the dermatoscope and talks with the patient
Dermatologist takes dermoscopy images
Dermatologist searches the image archive for earlier images of the same lesion
Dermatologist compares images and decides diagnosis and treatment
Dermatologist performs excisions and biopsies
Dermatologist writes examination findings and the treatment plan in the record

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the patient's consent, and the structured data in the record.
loop.output: A draft of the findings and plan in the record template.
loop.check: A check lists every statement in the draft that cannot be found in the consultation transcript, and every finding or plan item in the transcript missing from the draft; the dermatologist reads the draft against the consult, resolves each listed item and corrects every line before it is saved. A monthly sample audit looks for omissions.
loop.stop: The dermatologist writes it when the recording is incomplete or the patient declines recording.

steps.what: Dermatologist fills the pathology request
Dermatologist answers patient messages

tasks.design: Dermoscopy images are filed on a body map, so earlier images of the same lesion show beside the new one, instead of searching the archive. With consent, a certified scribe drafts the findings and plan, and the dermatologist corrects every draft before it is saved. Examining, imaging, deciding, surgery, the pathology request and messages stay with the dermatologist. No model reads the lesion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Earlier images were searched for by hand and notes typed after each visit.
tasks.enabler_now: Body-map image filing and certified ambient scribes.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing the ugly duckling among dozens of moles.
tasks.altitude: Less searching and typing; diagnosis stays.

reach.learn: Whether changes are compared with every earlier image.

evidence.claim: In a peer-reviewed study of 236,153 scribe notes, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes; three of seven authors were from the vendor.
A clinical scribe and coding tool carries MDR class IIa.
Ambient recording captures staff performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: diagnosing and treating pigmented lesions; ordering diagnostic tests (task 17084) is a sibling task.
s7 is part of conducting or ordering diagnostic tests, which sibling task 17084 covers; its saving is counted there.
The history part of the consultation note is task 17078 in this set; this step covers only the findings and plan, so the scribe saving is not counted twice.
s3 keeps 40 for images from before the body map; s6 is priced at 75.
unknowns: Share of patients who consent to recording.

already_counted.description: Dermatologist corrects drafted findings and plans.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most lesions still have images from before the body map (s3 keeps 70) and few patients agree to recording (s6 keeps 90) (1.8); high: the body map holds earlier images and most patients agree (4.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Counsel patients on dermatologic screenings, sun protection, skin cancer awareness and self-examination, demonstrate self-examination, give leaflets, note counselling, set annual screening recalls and answer follow-up messages.

steps.what: Dermatologist counsels patients on dermatologic screenings, sun protection and skin cancer awareness
Dermatologist demonstrates skin and lymph node self-examinations
Dermatologist selects leaflets: printed today, picked from vetted texts for the portal after the change
Dermatologist checks the leaflets fit this patient's risk and the advice given, and that they go to this patient
Dermatologist sends the checked leaflets to the patient portal
Dermatologist notes the counselling in the record

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the patient's consent, and the structured data in the record.
loop.output: A draft of the counselling note in the record template.
loop.check: A check lists every statement in the draft that cannot be found in the consultation transcript; the dermatologist reads the draft against the consult, resolves each listed statement and corrects every line before it is saved. A monthly sample audit looks for omissions.
loop.stop: The dermatologist writes it when the recording is incomplete or the patient declines recording.

steps.what: Dermatologist sets the annual screening recall in the record
Dermatologist writes replies to follow-up messages: from scratch today, from a draft citing vetted texts after the change

loop.input: The patient's question and vetted, guideline-based patient texts.
loop.output: A draft reply citing the text it draws on.
loop.check: Each reply sentence must cite its vetted paragraph. A second check reads each sentence against the cited paragraph and flags sentences the paragraph does not support; questions about new symptoms or not covered by the texts get no draft and the dermatologist answers them by hand.
loop.stop: Questions about the patient's own diagnosis go to the dermatologist unanswered.
loop.why_not_simpler: Patients ask in their own words.

steps.what: Dermatologist checks the final reply: advice against the patient's record and the vetted texts, and that it goes to this patient
Dermatologist sends the checked reply through the patient portal

tasks.design: Leaflets from vetted, guideline-based texts are chosen, checked and sent once to the patient portal. The annual screening recall is set automatically from the diagnosis code, and the dermatologist confirms it. With consent, the scribe drafts the counselling note. Follow-up replies start from drafts citing vetted texts; the dermatologist adapts each, checks the final reply and sends it once. Counselling and demonstration stay with the dermatologist.

approvals.approved_version: Each reply text exactly as checked by the dermatologist in s6c, sent once through the patient portal to the patient who asked; any change needs a new check.
The leaflets exactly as checked by the dermatologist in s3c, sent once to this patient's portal; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Leaflets were printed and recalls set by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Portal leaflets, coded recalls, scribes and reply drafting with citations.
tasks.still_hard: Patients who skip their annual screening.
tasks.human_edge: Persuading a sun-seeking patient to change habits.

evidence.claim: A patient information site is guideline-based and written with professional bodies and a patients' federation.
In a peer-reviewed study of 236,153 scribe notes, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes; three of seven authors were from the vendor.
Ambient recording captures staff performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: counselling on prevention; diagnosing and treating skin conditions (task 17095) is in this set and a separate task.
The means prior puts 2% on screens; the steps show 4%, for setting screening recalls, and slightly less in person.
s3 keeps half; s4 is priced at 75; s5 keeps 30 for confirming the recall; s6 keeps 70 because the dermatologist adapts every draft; the leaflet and reply checks and sends keep their full time.
research_questions: Do more patients attend annual screening?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few patients use the portal leaflets (s3 keeps 80), few agree to recording (s4 keeps 95) and few questions fit a draft (s6 keeps 95) (3.3); high: the design as priced (5.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Examine patients and discuss symptoms, decide diagnosis and plan, perform treatments, write findings and plan, prescribe, order tests, write, check and send the GP letter and answer patient messages to diagnose and treat skin conditions such as acne, psoriasis or skin cancer.

steps.what: Dermatologist examines patients and discusses symptoms of skin conditions such as acne, psoriasis or skin cancer
Dermatologist decides diagnosis and treatment plan
Dermatologist performs treatments such as cryotherapy, excisions and injections
Dermatologist writes examination findings and the treatment plan in the record

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the patient's consent, and the structured data in the record.
loop.output: A draft of the findings and plan in the record template.
loop.check: A check lists every statement in the draft that cannot be found in the consultation transcript, and every finding or plan item in the transcript missing from the draft; the dermatologist reads the draft against the consult, resolves each listed item and corrects every line before it is saved. A monthly sample audit looks for omissions.
loop.stop: The dermatologist writes it when the recording is incomplete or the patient declines recording.

steps.what: Dermatologist writes prescriptions in the prescribing system
Dermatologist orders laboratory tests
Dermatologist writes the letter to the GP
Dermatologist checks the final GP letter: findings, plan and medication against the record, and the patient's own GP as addressee
Dermatologist signs and sends the checked letter to the GP
Dermatologist answers patient messages

approvals.approved_version: The GP letter exactly as checked by the dermatologist in s8, signed and sent once to the patient's own GP; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: With consent, a certified scribe drafts the findings and plan, which the dermatologist corrects. The GP letter fills from the validated findings, plan and prescription, and the dermatologist edits, checks and signs it before it is sent. Examining, deciding, treating, prescribing, ordering tests and messages stay with the dermatologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes and letters were typed after each consultation.
tasks.enabler_now: Certified scribes and letters filled from validated notes.
tasks.still_hard: Complex patients whose letters need careful wording.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a treatment the patient will keep using.

evidence.claim: In a peer-reviewed study of 236,153 scribe notes, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes; three of seven authors were from the vendor.
A clinical scribe and coding tool carries MDR class IIa.
Ambient recording captures staff performance and needs works council consent.
A prescription comes from a named practitioner; drafting tools do not prescribe.

assumptions: Boundary: diagnosing and treating skin conditions; prescribing hormonal and topical agents (task 17089) and ordering diagnostic tests (task 17084) are sibling tasks.
s5 is part of prescribing hormonal agents or topical treatments, which sibling task 17089 covers; its saving is counted there.
s6 is part of conducting or ordering diagnostic tests, which sibling task 17084 covers; its saving is counted there.
The history part of the consultation note is task 17078 in this set; this step covers only the findings and plan, so the scribe saving is not counted twice.
s4 is priced at 75; s7 keeps 60 because every letter is edited.
research_questions: Do GP letters go out sooner?

already_counted.description: Dermatologist corrects drafted notes and letters.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few patients agree to recording (s4 keeps 92) and letters need heavy edits (s7 keeps 80) (1.4); high: most consults recorded and letters fill as designed (3.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Let patients fill a pre-visit questionnaire, review referral letters and earlier records, take the history, retype medication and allergies, copy questionnaire answers, write the history in the record and request missing records to record patients' health histories.

steps.what: Patient fills the pre-visit skin history questionnaire in the portal
Dermatologist reviews referral letters and earlier records
Dermatologist takes the health history in conversation with the patient
Dermatologist retypes medication and allergies from the referral letter into the record
Dermatologist copies questionnaire answers into the record
Dermatologist records patients' health histories in the record

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the patient's consent, and the structured data in the record.
loop.output: A draft of the health history in the record template.
loop.check: A check lists every statement in the draft that cannot be found in the consultation transcript or the questionnaire, and every item in the transcript missing from the draft; the dermatologist reads the draft against the consult, resolves each listed item and corrects every line before it is saved. A monthly sample audit looks for omissions.
loop.stop: The dermatologist writes it when the recording is incomplete or the patient declines recording.

steps.what: Dermatologist requests missing records from the GP by mail

tasks.design: Medication and allergies arrive by integration from the patient's medication overview, instead of retyping them from referral letters. Questionnaire answers flow into the record, instead of being copied. With consent, the scribe drafts the history, and the dermatologist corrects it before it is saved. Reviewing letters, taking the history and requesting records stay with the dermatologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Medication, answers and history were typed by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Medication integration, portal questionnaires feeding the record and certified scribes.
tasks.human_edge: Asking the question that uncovers the real trigger.

evidence.claim: In a peer-reviewed study of 236,153 scribe notes, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes; three of seven authors were from the vendor.
A clinical scribe and coding tool carries MDR class IIa.
Ambient recording captures staff performance and needs works council consent.
Health data are special category; expect a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: recording health histories; recommending diagnostic tests (task 17085) is a sibling task. This task carries the scribe saving for the history part of the note only.
Input contract for s4: about 60% of patients have a medication overview available by integration; s4 is priced at that share and keeps 40.
s5 saves copying answers the patient already entered and keeps 20 for checks; s6 is priced at 70.
The means prior puts 28% on documents; the steps show about 35%, because writing the history is the main desk work.
Patients' questionnaire time is shown in s1.
unknowns: Share of patients completing the questionnaire.
research_questions: Do medication errors in the record fall?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only a third of patients have an overview by integration (s4 keeps 70), half fill the questionnaire (s5 keeps 60) and few agree to recording (s6 keeps 90) (8.1); high: coverage as assumed (19.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
